gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could read states how many hours a bus-powered 16-inch 2560x1600 screen leaves a 16-inch MacBook Pro on battery: about 5.3 to 5.6 h against Apple's 17 h wireless-web figure at a 12-13 W rated screen, or how its 189 ppi compares with the MacBook's 254 ppi.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's best-for-Mac list (cited), PCWorld's list (cited) and both rottenwifi pages. Macworld gives only 'Laptop battery drain' as an espresso Pro con and '65W pass-through charging' for the Float 2 Pro, with no monitor wattage, no hours and no ppi. PCWorld gives pass-through wattages only and no battery statement. rottenwifi says QHD 'is usually easier on the battery than 4K OLED' and states 'no battery-hour figures' and no ppi. ChatGPT's own answers say a bus-powered monitor shortens battery life and that pass-through may not be enough, with no number. Not compared: the RTINGS page returned navigation only and the TechRadar page was truncated after its first pick, so I cannot say what those two state.
decides: It confirms the 2560x1600 line over 1920x1200 with a number (74% of the MacBook's pixel density against 56%) but does not by itself reorder the 120 Hz candidates. On rated power the stacked Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro (7.5 W on a retailer listing) leaves about 7.5 h against about 5.3 to 5.6 h for 12-13 W side screens, which supports it for the stacked segment, with the caveat that the 7.5 W may be a low-brightness figure. I could not open the UPERFECT or SOTSU store pages today (HTTP 429 on every attempt), so there are no derived figures or prices for the GR16EQ, GR16DQ or FlipAction Pro 16 Gen 2. One caution for a UPERFECT pick: Parkablogs measured 238 nits on the 2023 UPlays C2 against 400 advertised, and says macOS needs BetterDisplay for sharp scaling at this resolution.

findings.label: 16-inch MacBook Pro average draw in Apple's wireless-web test (M5 Pro)
findings.note: 100 Wh battery / 17 h wireless web = 5.88 W. Apple lists 16 h for M5 Max (6.25 W) and 24 h video streaming for M5 Pro. Same page: 16.2-inch 3456x2234 at 254 ppi, up to 120 Hz, 4.7 lb, 140 W adapter, M5 Pro drives up to 3 external displays and M5 Max up to 4.

findings.label: MacBook Pro 16 battery hours with the screen bus-powered at its rated ceiling
findings.value: at least about 5.3 h (vs 17 h alone)
findings.note: ASUS: 'Power Consumption : <13W'. 100 Wh / (5.88 W + 13 W) = 5.30 h. An estimate, not a test: Apple's figure has no external display, the extra GPU load of a second screen is not counted, and 13 W is the ceiling. Same page: 16-inch 2560x1600, 500 cd/m2 typical, 1.2 kg (2.65 lb), 2x USB-C DP Alt Mode + HDMI 2.0.

findings.label: MacBook Pro 16 battery hours with the screen bus-powered at rated power
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Teoh Yi Chie, Parkablogs, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: Spec list in the review: 'Rated Power: 12W'. 100 Wh / (5.88 W + 12 W) = 5.59 h. 12 W is 2.0x the MacBook's own 5.88 W average (12 / 5.88 = 2.04). This is the 2023 model, not the GR16DQ page; its 12 W and 0.72 kg match the desk lead for the GR16DQ, which I could not open today.

findings.label: MacBook Pro 16 battery hours with the screen bus-powered at listed maximum power
findings.source_title: Central Computer listing, Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro (part 101-1011P03)
findings.note: Retailer listing: 'Maximum Power Consumption 7.50 W'. 100 Wh / (5.88 W + 7.5 W) = 7.47 h. Treat as a best case: a search snippet of the Float 2 manual says 7.5 W is at the default 20% brightness and rises above it, but I could not read the manual text myself. Same listing: 2560x1600, 120 Hz, 350 nit, 2.90 lb.

Pixel density of a 16-inch 1920x1200 panel against the MacBook Pro 16 (the screens left below the line)
Workspace of a 2560x1600 panel at clean 2x scaling against the MacBook Pro 16 at 2x
findings.note: Half of 3456x2234 is 1728x1117; half of 2560x1600 is 1280x800; (1280 x 800) / (1728 x 1117) = 1,024,000 / 1,930,176 = 0.53. At 1x the panel shows 2560x1600 points with UI at 127 / 188.7 = 67% of the MacBook's physical size (127 = 254 / 2).

findings.label: Teoh Yi Chie (Parkablogs) on macOS scaling and measured brightness
findings.value: 238 nits measured max against 400 advertised; 'MacOS users will need an app called BetterDisplay for proper (sharp) UI scaling'
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Teoh Yi Chie, Parkablogs, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: Also: 'MacOS does not work well with QHD & QHD+ resolution on a 16-inch display'. 238 / 400 = 60% of the claim. This is the 2023 unit, not the current GR16EQ (450 cd/m2 claimed per the desk lead) or GR16DQ.

findings.label: Carry weight with a 16-inch MacBook Pro
findings.note: Macworld: 2.9 lb (1.3 kg); Apple: 4.7 lb. 4.7 + 2.9 = 7.6 lb; 2.9 / 4.7 = 0.62. Macworld also lists 16-inch, 2560x1600, 120 Hz, 350 nits, reviewed at $299.99.

Carry weight with a 16-inch MacBook Pro
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Teoh Yi Chie, Parkablogs, 2023-06-20)
findings.note: Review spec list: net 0.72 kg (1.59 lb), panel without folio. 4.7 + 1.59 = 6.29 lb; 1.59 / 4.7 = 0.34.

findings.label: Pass-through charging against the MacBook Pro 16's own adapter
findings.note: Macworld: '65W pass-through charging'; Apple specs: 140W USB-C power adapter. 65 / 140 = 0.46. The Parkablogs review says the 2023 UPlays C2 passes 'less than 10W', so it 'can't really charge a laptop through the display'.

findings.label: What the readable rival pages say on battery and pixel density
findings.value: Macworld: 'Laptop battery drain' (espresso Pro con) only; rottenwifi: '1080p or QHD is usually easier on the battery than 4K OLED', no hours and no ppi; PCWorld: no battery-drain statement
findings.source_title: Best Portable Monitors for MacBooks in 2026: USB-C, 4K & OLED (rottenwifi)
findings.note: Also read today: https://www.macworld.com/article/2836233/best-portable-monitors-for-mac.html, https://www.pcworld.com/article/1787210/best-portable-monitors.html and https://rottenwifi.com/best-portable-monitors-for-your-mac-in-2026/ (its only 16-inch 2560x1600 pick, the ViewSonic TD1656-2K, is 60 Hz). Of the 16-inch 2560x1600 120 Hz candidates, only the Duex Float 2 Pro appears on these pages (Macworld and rottenwifi).

unsourced: UPERFECT GR16EQ and GR16DQ rated power, weight, brightness and today's price: uperfect.com returned HTTP 429 on every attempt (storecheck six times, WebFetch twice), so no battery-hour, weight or cost figure is derived for either current model. The 12 W and 0.72 kg used above come from the 2023 UPlays C2 review.

SOTSU FlipAction Pro 16 Gen 2 power, weight and price: sotsu.com returned HTTP 429, and the B&H and Adorama pages returned 403. A search snippet of the B&H listing showed 'Maximum: 11.0 W', which would give 100 / (5.88 + 11) = 5.9 h, but I did not open the page.

Mobile Pixels Duex Float 2 Pro wattage from the maker: mobilepixels.us returned HTTP 429, and the Float 2 & 2 Pro manual PDF (content.etilize.com/User-Manual/1086290168.pdf) downloaded but its text could not be extracted here. The 7.5 W is a retailer listing's figure.
Mobile Pixels Fold 16 QHD power draw: not looked up within the call budget, so no battery-hour figure.
ASUS ZenScreen MB16QHG refresh rate and US price or stock: the ASUS tech-spec page I opened lists neither.
